newsitem.title: GERMANY: German wheat prices consolidate recent gains.
newsitem.headline: German wheat prices consolidate recent gains.

text.p: German wheat export prices have consolidated recent gains but the upside is now limited amid competitive pressure and sluggish demand, brokers said on Wednesday.
Ports were busy handling recent intervention rye and barley sales to third countries and this had delayed the execution of wheat sales to southern Europe and Poland, they said.
"This means there won't be any quick follow-on sales," one said, adding British and French sellers were also active.
Some 95 percent of the wheat crop in northern Germany has now been harvested, showing good hagberg numbers and high protein content, which underpinned prices.
Feed wheat prices were undermined by competitive British offers but benefited from higher soymeal prices, which encouraged feed grain use.

The Hamburg grain exchange this week raised its new crop bread wheat price (12.5 percent, 220 hagberg) by 2.50 marks to 287.50 marks, but cut its spot feed wheat price free Hamburg by two marks to 275.00 marks.
The fob bread wheat offer range was steady at 290-320 marks but brokers said sellers' resolve was weakening, otherwise they would have hiked prices to reflect storage since the harvest.
Domestic barley free delivered Hamburg was offered at 255 marks a tonne but traded prices were just 248.50 marks because of slack demand.
Malting barley was offered at 300 marks compared with 320 marks in pre-harvest fixed contracts and prices were set to weaken under supply pressure.
Spot export barley remained at 250-260 marks fob, bread rye just under 260 marks fob and feed rye at 245 marks fob.
